author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: this bead's fix path spans 5 extension-client crates, not just calendars. The bead body explicitly says 'sweep mail-client first, then propagate per the canonical-template rule', meaning the fix should:

1. Add ifFromInState, ifInState (and verify onSuccessDestroyOriginal, destroyFromIfInState) to canonical mail-client EmailCopyParams.
2. Cookie-cut a new CalendarEventCopyParams type in calendars-client.
3. Propagate the new field shape to the 3 other extension-client siblings that have /copy methods: tasks-client (Task/copy), contacts-client (ContactCard/copy), filenode-client (FileNode/copy).
4. Update each crate's smoke tests.

That is workspace-wide canonical-template propagation, which AGENTS.md treats as a first-order workspace change requiring deliberate scoping. The current bead JMAP-1j9k.13 is shaped as a single-crate finding.

Options:
(a) Open a new sweep epic ('RFC 8620 §5.4 /copy args canonical sweep across extension-client family') with 5 children, one per crate, and close JMAP-1j9k.13 as superseded.
(b) Take the workspace AGENTS.md 'do not over-engineer; only touch files within the task's stated scope' rule literally and fix only calendars-client to the bead's exact spec — creating a knowing canonical-divergence (calendars-client EmailCopyParams equivalent has more fields than mail-client's EmailCopyParams), with an explicit note in the canonical mail-client PLAN.md that a sweep is pending.
(c) Fix the canonical (mail-client) AND only calendars (not tasks/contacts/filenode), accepting incomplete propagation as a known follow-up.

My recommendation: option (a). It matches the bead author's own 'if accepted, sweep mail-client first, then propagate' guidance, avoids creating canonical-template drift in either direction, and reorganises the work into the scope shape the rest of the workspace uses. The 5 child beads should each be small and independently committable.

Skipping JMAP-1j9k.13 in the /do-beads loop and continuing to the next ready bead.
